title: Molle Mystery Theatre
paragraphs: A mystery and suspense anthology presenting standalone crime and thriller dramas, often framed by the program's criminologist-commentator Geoffrey Barnes.

NBC mystery/suspense anthology built around standalone literary and original crime dramas. The recurring criminologist-commentator Geoffrey Barnes framed many broadcasts; Peter Lorre and other celebrity hosts also appear in surviving programs.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Early NBC Mystery Theatre (September 7, 1943 to December 21, 1943) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Molle Mystery Theatre NBC era (December 28, 1943 to June 25, 1948) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|bernard-lenrow|Bernard Lenrow]] (host and performer), Dan Seymour (announcer, commercial spokesman, and performer), Alexander Semmler (composer and conductor), Peter Lorre (host), Cornell Woolrich (writer, author, and performer), Jack Miller (music, composer, and conductor), and George Putnam (announcer and commercial spokesman).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to murder and homicide, psychological fear, obsession and madness, blackmail, greed and coercion, courtroom, jury and legal jeopardy, supernatural, occult and haunting, and poisoning and toxic murder methods.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes AFRS Mystery Playhouse redistribution, Sponsor-branded network mystery, and Literary mystery adaptation culture.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]], [[show|the-shadow|The Shadow]], and [[show|inner-sanctum-mysteries|Inner Sanctum Mysteries]].
